problem_statement: The fire-trails project is a Vite + Three.js interactive WebGL scene: a fullscreen WebGLRenderer canvas with OrbitControls, Tweakpane Fire/Particles controls, three render targets, a pointer-driven trail simulation, and real GLSL fire/ground/particle shaders. Over the fullscreen canvas the page mounts the demo's own on-scene 'Shader pass inspector' HUD: a compact translucent panel with a Vite pipeline marker, a filter chip row (All passes / Fire / Ground / Particles / Trail), a live readout, and a grid of four render-pass tiles (Fire 50 x 50 fire plane, Ground rt1 rt2 rt3, Particles 60 x 60 grid, Trail uUVPointer trail). Clicking a chip focuses that render pass: it dims the non-focused tiles, rewrites the readout to 'Inspecting: <Pass> - N of 4 passes', and tags the inspector with a per-pass context class so the focused pass is identifiable. Two defects were reported. (1) On a 390px mobile phone the inspector's chip row and tile grid are a fixed-width non-wrapping strip, so the whole page scrolls sideways (about 357px wider than the viewport); desktop and tablet look fine. (2) The pass-focus control is mis-wired: clicking a chip flips its active state but the live readout and the per-pass context class do not update, so the inspector reports a stale pass and count. Repair the pass-inspector so the chip row and tile grid wrap with no horizontal overflow on 390px mobile AND clicking a pass chip updates both the live readout ('Inspecting: <Pass> - N of 4 passes') and the per-pass context class, while leaving the fullscreen WebGL canvas, OrbitControls, Tweakpane controls, render targets, the pointer trail, the render loop, and the shader imports exactly as they are.
required_content: Fix the layout so the 390px mobile page has no horizontal overflow (document scroll width must not exceed the viewport beyond a small tolerance).
Repair the styling and wiring in the source files (src/pass-inspector.css and src/pass-inspector.js), not by editing generated dist output only.

Keep every render-pass tile visible and readable: Fire, Ground, Particles, and Trail, in the dark/fire visual language with legible warm-on-dark text (no illegible dark-on-dark contrast, no overlapping shingled tiles).

Clicking a filter chip must update the live readout to 'Inspecting: <Pass> - N of 4 passes' and add the matching pass-inspector--<pass> context class so the focused render pass is identifiable. For example, clicking the Fire chip updates the readout to 'Inspecting: Fire' (with its live pass count) and focuses the Fire pass.

Use the local Vite marker asset /vite.svg visibly in the inspector header and preserve the fullscreen WebGL canvas, Tweakpane Fire/Particles controls, OrbitControls, render targets, and pointer-driven trail rendering.
Do not remove or restructure the WebGL scene, the Tweakpane panel, the render loop, or the shader imports while fixing the overflow and the pass-focus wiring.
Ground the repair in the existing dark fire visual language: warm orange accents, smoky black background, small technical labels, and no decorative unrelated imagery.
design_constraints: Keep the existing dark/fire visual language: warm orange accents, smoky black background, compact translucent panel, small technical labels, and no decorative unrelated imagery.

The fix is a source-level responsive + interaction repair of the on-scene pass-inspector HUD that floats over the fullscreen canvas, not a replacement hero, modal, new route, remote panel, or detached custom app.
Do not edit shader math, render-target swapping, the requestAnimationFrame loop, OrbitControls setup, or Tweakpane bindings while fixing the inspector.

Desktop, tablet, and 390px mobile states must have no horizontal overflow after the repair, and the inspector must remain visually intact and legible on desktop with the canvas still visible and clickable.
state_constraints: desktop_initial and desktop_inspector check the WebGL canvas plus the pass-inspector HUD render as a clean, legible, non-overlapping panel with no horizontal overflow on desktop.

desktop_pass_fire / desktop_pass_ground / desktop_pass_particles click a filter chip and check the readout updates to the focused pass and the inspector gains the matching pass-inspector--<pass> context class.
desktop_canvas_center and desktop_canvas_corner click the fullscreen canvas to exercise the pointer/trail state without removing the inspector, confirming the WebGL interaction still works.
tablet_initial checks an intermediate viewport with no horizontal overflow.
mobile_initial and mobile_inspector check the 390px mobile page: the reference wraps the chip row and tile grid so there is no horizontal overflow; the unrepaired baseline overflows.

change_completion: The 390px mobile page (mobile_initial and mobile_inspector) has no horizontal overflow after the repair.
Clicking a filter chip updates the live readout to 'Inspecting: <Pass> - N of 4 passes' instead of leaving it stale.
design_consistency: The repaired inspector keeps the dark fire visual language: warm orange accents, translucent smoky panel, small uppercase technical labels, and legible warm-on-dark text.
The fix extends src/pass-inspector.css and src/pass-inspector.js (source files) rather than bypassing the build pipeline or merely clipping overflow.
responsive: Desktop, tablet, and 390px mobile states have no horizontal overflow.
The render-pass tiles wrap and remain readable and fully visible on 390px mobile while the canvas stays visible and clickable.
regression: The WebGLRenderer canvas, Tweakpane Fire/Particles controls, OrbitControls desktop setup, pointer trail, render loop, and shader imports remain intact.
The patch does not add a backend, new framework, remote panel, or rewrite the shader scene.
evaluation_rubric.scoring_notes: A correct patch is a small source-level responsive + interaction repair of the pass-inspector HUD. Patches that merely clip overflow (overflow-x:hidden while keeping a fixed-width nowrap strip), shingle the tiles into an overlapping dark-on-dark pile, leave the readout/context class stale on click, edit dist only, remove the inspector, or break the WebGL canvas should fail the no-overflow, visual-regression, cross-context, or interaction checks.
